name: Label text to class ID resolution on import
answer:
ANSWERED BY DECISION 6, which the owner approved: keep legacy per-image class ids and aliases. No project-wide class list.

Both questions on the card therefore get the same answer. Class names do NOT map to a stable project-wide list, and per-file renumbering IS accepted for a dataset labelled only in Pascal VOC or CreateML. The reason is not that the defect is imaginary - it is real and the card describes it correctly - but that fixing it would break the thing decision 6 exists to protect. Exported ids must match legacy exports byte for byte, and a project label map changes which id a name resolves to, so every export in the dataset would shift.

WHAT THIS COSTS, stated plainly so it is a known cost rather than a surprise. A dataset whose only annotations are name-based (VOC or CreateML) has no stable id space: 'car' can be class 1 in one image and class 2 in the next, depending on what else appears in that file and in what order. Training on such a dataset without re-mapping produces silently wrong labels. That is legacy behaviour and the port reproduces it.

WHAT MITIGATES IT, and belongs in Phase 4. The alias table the user has already built is consulted BEFORE the fallback, so a name that matches a known alias keeps its id. The gap only opens for names the session has never seen. So the dataset browser should carry the alias table across images within a session rather than rebuilding it per file, which costs nothing and closes most of the instability in practice.

A project label map may be layered on later as an optional VIEW, exactly as decision 6 says: a mapping applied when reading for training, leaving the files untouched. That is a feature, not a fix to this rule.
